protocol: Do not delete or reclassify canonical source records, do not remove shortlisted IDs without explicit composition update, and do not turn explanatory app/implementation metadata into discoveries. These are editorial route recommendations, not claim approval.

decisions.rationale: Generic posture caveat; not surprising or source-particular, and local custom should be handled by user settings rather than a Home discovery.
Description largely duplicates the sanctuary-lamp definition; fuel variance requires qualified canon-law explanation.
Stoup-versus-font is useful glossary context but repeats the purpose of the original entry.
The 25 April Greater Litany and pre-Ascension Lesser Litanies offer a concrete calendar-based discovery, distinct from unsupported assumptions about a local procession.

proposed_home_copy_not_applied.en: In the 1962 Roman calendar, the Greater Litanies are assigned to 25 April, while the Lesser Litanies normally fall on the three days before Ascension.
proposed_home_copy_not_applied.fr: Dans le calendrier romain de 1962, les Grandes Litanies sont fixées au 25 avril, tandis que les Petites Litanies ont normalement lieu les trois jours précédant l'Ascension.

decisions.rationale: Historical source confirms O salutaris is drawn from two concluding stanzas of Thomas Aquinas's larger Corpus Christi hymn; discard app-internal 'Latin phrase object' language.

proposed_home_copy_not_applied.en: O salutaris Hostia is not a separate hymn originally: its two stanzas come from the end of Saint Thomas Aquinas's Verbum supernum prodiens.
proposed_home_copy_not_applied.fr: O salutaris Hostia n'était pas à l'origine un hymne indépendant : ses deux strophes proviennent de la fin du Verbum supernum prodiens de saint Thomas d'Aquin.

decisions.rationale: The pyx's portability and communion-to-sick use are already essentially in the glossary definition; not novel enough independently.
Distinguishing ciborium, chalice, and humeral veils is glossary taxonomy, without an independently compelling source anecdote.
The historical name of the sacrament and its explicit treatment by Trent can make a clear discovery; remove internal glossary-scope explanation.

proposed_home_copy_not_applied.en: The Council of Trent explicitly taught that Extreme Unction is a sacrament instituted by Christ, drawing on Saint James's instruction about anointing the sick.
proposed_home_copy_not_applied.fr: Le concile de Trente enseigna explicitement que l'Extrême-Onction est un sacrement institué par le Christ, en s'appuyant sur l'enseignement de saint Jacques au sujet de l'onction des malades.
proposed_home_copy_not_applied.secondary_citation: Council of Trent, Session XIV, On Extreme Unction, chapter I
